problems.stem: Your future learning plan lists the goal 'Get better at coding.' Why will this goal be hard to act on or check?
options: It is too short to be a goal.
It has no measurable outcome or deadline, so you cannot tell when it is met; 'Publish a 3-page HTML site by August 1' is checkable.
Coding is not a CAT 100 topic.
problems.explanation: A usable goal is measurable and dated. 'Get better' has no finish line; a concrete deliverable with a date does.

problems.stem: Your plan has the milestone 'Understand Excel formulas.' What turns it into a milestone a reviewer can verify?
options: Attach a proof: 'Build a budget file that uses SUMIFS and VLOOKUP across 200 rows and post the file link.'
Move it to the end of the list.
Remove the deadline so there is less pressure.
problems.explanation: Each milestone needs an attached deliverable. A finished file using named functions is proof; 'understand Excel' is not checkable.

problems.stem: You ask an AI tool for a learning plan and it returns ten advanced topics (databases, machine learning, cloud deploy, cybersecurity, and more) all for next month. What is the disciplined response?
options: Accept all ten; the AI knows the field better than you.
Reject the unrealistic scope, sequence by prerequisite, and pick one solid next step such as mastering spreadsheet formulas before databases.
Do the topics in alphabetical order.
Drop the plan because it is too hard.
problems.explanation: You judge the AI proposal against realism and prerequisites. A sequenced, achievable next step beats ten unordered advanced topics.

problems.stem: Which future-learning-plan row is specific, measurable, dated, and tied to proof?
options: 'Goal: publish a portfolio site. Proof: 3 pages live on GitHub Pages with valid HTML. Date: Aug 1. Prereq: finish CAT 100 HTML unit first.'
problems.explanation: A strong row names the goal, the measurable proof, the date, and the prerequisite, so progress can be tracked and verified.
